newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS ACQUIRE GILMOUR FROM LEAFS IN FIVE-PLAYER DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS ACQUIRE GILMOUR FROM LEAFS IN FIVE-PLAYER DEAL.

text.p: The Toronto Maples Leafs on Tuesday traded their popular captain Doug Gilmour to the New Jersey Devils as part of a five-player deal.

The Devils announced that they have acquired veteran centre Gilmour and defenceman Dave Ellett from the Maple Leafs for defenceman Jason Smith, forward Steve Sullivan and minor-league forward Alyn McCauley.

The struggling Maple Leafs -- 23-36-2 and tied with Boston and San Jose with a league-worst 48 points -- had been shopping the 33-year-old Gilmour, who has 15 goals and stood second on the team in scoring with 60 points.

"There is no question this makes us a better team," Devils general manager Lou Lamoriello said of acquiring Gilmour, a two-way player who led the Maple Leafs to the Western Conference finals in 1993 and 1994.
"It gives us better opportunity to win night in and night out," Lamoriello said.

New Jersey is currently tied with Florida for the third best record in the Eastern Conference on 70 points, but has been struggling offensively all season. Their 156 goals scored is second lowest in the league.

Gilmour joined the Maple Leafs in a 10-player trade with Calgary in January 1992. The following season he set single-season club records for points (127) and assists (95) and won the Selke Award as the NHL's top defensive forward.

Gilmour began his career with St Louis and was a key member of the Calgary team that defeated Montreal in the 1989 Stanley Cup Finals. In 1,052 career games, he has 361 goals and 740 goals for 1,101 points.
Ellett, 32, has four goals and 10 assists in 56 games in his 13th NHL season.
The Maple Leafs got considerably younger with Tuesday's trade.
The 23-year-old Smith was a first-round draft pick of the Devils in 1992. The 6-foot-3 (1.90 m), 205-pound (93 kg) defenceman has one goal and two assists in 57 games.
Sullivan, 22, had eight goals and 14 assists in 33 games.
